newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dollar slide weighs on DAX, but Wall St supports.
newsitem.headline: Dollar slide weighs on DAX, but Wall St supports.

text.p: German shares bowed to the pressure of a weaker dollar on Wednesday after the U.S. currency dropped from a 34-month high against the mark, but Wall Street's overnight advance helped stabilise the market.
In early bourse trade, the 30-share DAX index was down 35.04 points, more than one percent, at 3,241.12, as it caught up with a sharp slide in prices in after-bourse screen trade Tuesday.
However the IBIS DAX index, which already reflects late Tuesday trade, was up 11.53 points at 3,244.41 and March DTB DAX futures were up 14.5 points at 3,252.

"Everyone is waiting for a consolidation, and that's why it's just not coming," commented one Frankfurt dealer, who attributed the declines to a swift bout of dollar-driven profit-taking, which could be rapidly reversed.
The biggest decliners included insurance giant Allianz AG Holding, which was down 58 marks at 3,265 marks in early trade.

Allianz has been a strong performer in recent weeks after several significant earnings upgrades. The insurer is due to release preliminary 1996 earnings data later Wednesday and analysts expect a double-digit rise in pre-tax profit.

In the banking sector, lately also an outperformer as its 1996 earnings season gets into full swing, prices came under some pressure. Recent favourite Bayerische Hypotheken und Wechsel Bank AG, also due to report profits today, was down 1.10 marks at 51.40.
German share traders will be keeping a watchful eye on U.S. data due later today, including January consumer price data.
"Wall Street is key. I believe it is due a downward correction in the coming week and if so, the DAX will follow," another dealer said.
